title: Ghost striping: adaptive KV shard migration for tensor/pipeline continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a novel 'ghost striping' mechanism for KV cache placement that performs low-latency, adaptive migration of hot KV entries across GPUs while preserving pipeline/tensor parallel locality and respecting continuous batching windows. The goal is to reduce remote KV fetches and cross-GPU synchronization during sustained streaming workloads without causing pipeline stalls or large memory copy spikes.
background: We currently use static slab/stripe mappings for KV slices which work well for steady-state distributions but suffer when hotkeys shift between micro-batches or when tensor/pipeline parallel topology causes an uneven hotspot on a subset of devices. Continuous batching amplifies transient hotkey patterns (prefix-heavy requests, conversational turn changes), producing cross-GPU traffic and periodic latency spikes. Existing sharding tickets explored striping, prefetched spill tiers, and micropartitioning; this ticket experiments with ephemeral ghost replicas and graded migration to smooth transitions.
proposed_solution: Implement an adaptive ghost-striping layer: each GPU maintains lightweight ghost replicas (compact, read-only KV headers + small top-K value cache) for remote hotkeys observed in the recent batching window. When a ghost's access rate exceeds a threshold, we perform a graded migration: first promote a small value cache to the target device and update routing metadata in a best-effort manner; on sustained hotness, perform a full ownership transfer with coordinated handoff respecting tensor/pipeline stage boundaries. Migration decisions use continuous-batching telemetry (batch size distribution, per-batch hotkey counts) and a cost model that predicts latency vs memory tradeoffs.
technical_details: Ghost structure: 64-byte header per key (key hash, kv-size-estimate, recent-access-score) + optional small LRU value store for up to N entries (configurable), stored in pinned GPU memory region separate from primary slab allocations.

Telemetry: integrate with the batching controller to emit per-batch hotkey histograms and per-GPU access rates. Use exponentially-weighted moving averages (EWMA) to track hotness over the last M batches.

Thresholds & grading: two thresholds: ghost-promote-threshold (create small replica), migrate-threshold (start ownership transfer). Migrate operation includes: allocate destination slab space, copy KV-value (asynchronously via P2P/NCCL where available), update RSM-managed placement map, and drain in-flight references with epoch tags tied to the batching window.

Tensor/pipeline awareness: prefer to migrate KV shards to GPUs that are on the same tensor/pipeline parallel stage as the requesting operators to minimize cross-stage communication. The placement policy consults the runtime view of tensor splits and pipeline boundaries.

Consistency & handoff: use epoched routing entries and a short-lived dual-read window where both old owner and new owner answer reads; writes are serialized to the new owner after migration completes. For safety, we fall back to the previous owner for any uncertain requests until the epoch advances and old caches are expired.

Cost model: online estimator combining predicted per-token overhead (ms) for remote fetch vs additional memory footprint. Migration initiated only if expected P90 latency reduction > configured delta and memory headroom exists on target GPU.
Prefetch hints: integrate with prefix cache heuristics from batching controller to pre-create ghosts for keys likely to be accessed in subsequent micro-batches (use n-gram prefix signals).

Spill/fallback: if target GPU cannot host full value, ghost remains read-only and a warm-prefetch attempt is scheduled. If memory pressure rises, perform LRU demotion of ghosts before evicting primary slabs.

Observability: expose metrics: ghost_count_per_gpu, ghost_promote_rate, migrations_started/completed, migration_copy_latency, p90_remote-kv-latency before/after migration, additional memory-used-by-ghosts.
Implementation roadmap: runtime changes in shard-orchestrator + KV manager (C++), batching controller telemetry hooks (Go/Python), placement policy module (configurable via Console).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit tests, integration tests in CI and microbench harness. Phase 1 (canary): enable ghost-striping on internal dev clusters with synthetic conversational load and 4-node tensor/pipeline setups. Observe metrics for 48 hours. Phase 2 (staged): 10% production traffic for low-risk tenant group with opt-in. Phase 3: global enable with autotuning defaults. Use runtime-1.19 canary channel for initial deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Ghost-striping implemented and compiled in runtime branch with feature flag guard
Integration tests showing no increase in per-batch tail latency > 5% for baseline workloads
Under synthetic hotkey churn scenarios, p95 remote-KV fetches reduced by >= 40% compared to static striping
Migration success rate >= 99.5% with median migration copy latency < 10ms on GPU P2P networks
Monitoring dashboards added to Console: ghost metrics and migration traces
Design doc and rollout plan reviewed by Storage and Serving runtime leads
Performance regression run against runtime-1.18 baseline prior to release
testing_plan: Unit tests for ghost lifecycle, simulated migrator that injects hotkey patterns, end-to-end integration using the microbatch harness (different TP/PP topologies), and chaos tests where migrations are interrupted. Add a benchmark measuring throughput and token latency for streaming conversations with shifting hotkeys. Validate behavior on heterogeneous GPU families (A100, H100) and on setups without P2P to ensure copy fallback correctness.
risks_mitigation: Risk: migration causes pipeline stalls if not coordinated -> Mitigation: perform migrations at batching-epoch boundaries, limit concurrent migrations per pipeline stage
Risk: memory fragmentation from temporary ghost allocations -> Mitigation: reuse ghost arenas and apply compaction during low-load windows
Risk: mispredictions lead to oscillation (hotkey ping-pong) -> Mitigation: add dampening windows (cooldown) and require sustained hotness metric before full transfer
Risk: additional GPU memory overhead -> Mitigation: configurable global cap and per-GPU caps; prefer tiny ghost footprints initially
Risk: interaction with Dedicated customer capacity constraints -> Mitigation: placement policy respects reserved capacities and will not migrate into capacity-constrained pools
notes: This approach tries to balance low-latency streaming requirements with memory safety. Ghosts intentionally keep a tiny value-set to cover most small-key hot accesses and avoid triggering full value transfers for transient spikes. The term 'ghost' is inspired by ephemeral shadow replicas used in distributed systems (not related to OS ghost pages).
